- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% of recent mean.
- Model consistently over-estimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 2–5% after such events.
- Model under-estimates prices during prolonged downward trends (e.g., 5+ days of negative sentiment); add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–2% for the final 5–7 days if sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillations (e.g., +0.20, -0.20, +0.20), model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
